source.title: Do I Know This Entity? Knowledge Awareness and Hallucinations in Language Models
source.authors: Javier Ferrando; O. Obeso; Senthooran Rajamanoharan; Neel Nanda

record.file_problem: none noted; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper cites the harmful-refusal direction work and uses its weight-orthogonalization procedure as a comparison, but tests entity-recognition directions on knowledge refusal about factual entities, not safety refusal to harmful user requests.
record.gate_note: The paper explicitly distinguishes its knowledge refusal measure (declining factual questions due to lack of information) from safety refusal. Its steering and orthogonalization results therefore do not measure the behavior named by any claim version. The refusal figures separate entity types; refusal-rate values are presented graphically, while the text gives only qualitative summaries. Other reported findings about entity recognition, attention, and uncertainty are not results on the claim’s safety-refusal behavior.
record.test_reason: The paper borrows Arditi et al.'s weight orthogonalization and steering as tools, applied to SAE entity-recognition directions, and measures knowledge refusal (declining factual questions for lack of information, explicitly 'rather than safety concerns'). It finds no harmful-minus-harmless direction, uses no harmful requests, and reports no safety-refusal rates, so none of V1–V8 is tested. The reader's T4/uses_without_test classification is correct.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is essentially correct. The authors conclude that SAE latents found in the base model encode entity recognition (knowledge awareness) and causally control the chat model's knowledge refusal versus hallucination. They take this as evidence that chat finetuning repurposes an existing mechanism. The latents also regulate attention of attribute-extraction heads, and separate 'uncertainty' latents predict wrong answers.
record.recipe_differences: The paper finds entity-recognition SAE decoder directions based on known/unknown entity activation separation, rather than a harmful-minus-harmless mean-activation direction. It applies activation steering and weight orthogonalization to knowledge refusal.
record.method_sensitivity: Effects vary by model: the paper describes Gemma 2 2B effects as more pronounced than Gemma 2 9B. For Llama 3.1 8B, original refusal on unknown-entity prompts is high, and the known-entity latent does not produce a corresponding refusal decrease on known-entity prompts. Results are plotted separately by entity type.

fits_no_version.finding: Base-model SAE entity-recognition latents steer knowledge refusal in chat models (Gemma 2 2B/9B IT, Llama 3.1 8B). Steering with the unknown latent induces near-100% refusal in 2B. Orthogonalizing weights against the unknown-entity direction largely reduces refusal. Known-latent steering slightly reduces refusal in Gemma 2B but not in Llama.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Knowledge (non-safety) refusal in chat models is steerable via entity-recognition directions inherited from the base model, analogous to the single refusal direction.

record.problems: The measured behavior is string-matched factual knowledge refusal, not harmful-request safety refusal. Refusal rates are shown in figures without type-specific numeric values in the text. The study does not test whether general capabilities are preserved after intervention.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-relevant safety-refusal results exist. The paper’s separate attention, entity-classification, and uncertainty-direction analyses are omitted because they measure other outcomes. Refusal figures are retained by model and entity type; random-latent control rows are included for the two Gemma models, while no random-steering rows are retained for Llama 3.1 8B because of the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: No harmful-vs-harmless difference-in-means direction, no safety refusal, and no capability check.
Orthogonalization targets an entity-recognition direction and is scored on knowledge refusal, not safety refusal.
No jailbreaks and no adversarial training.
No analysis of the geometry of the safety-refusal representation.
Base-to-chat transfer is shown only for entity-recognition SAE latents acting on knowledge refusal, not for a safety-refusal direction.

record.verdict_notes: Arditi et al. is cited only as the source of the orthogonalization method and as motivation. The text says weight orthogonalization on every residual-writing matrix gives 'a large reduction in refusal responses' for knowledge refusal, which is an analogous but distinct behaviour. Llama random-steering control rows are omitted from the record, as the reader declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: No harmful-versus-harmless difference-in-means direction, harmful-request refusal, or general-capability preservation test.
Weight orthogonalization is applied to an entity-recognition direction and measured on knowledge refusal, not safety refusal or abliteration of safety refusal.
No jailbreak suppression of a safety-refusal direction or training against its ablation.
No test of whether harmful-request refusal is represented by an affine set, cone, or multiple refusal directions.
No separation of harmfulness judgment from safety-refusal decisions.
Cross-model effects concern entity-recognition directions and knowledge refusal, not transfer of a safety-refusal direction or behavior.
No comparison of safety-refusal training regimes or training timing.
